rule: append-only; records point at superseded nested keys without touching the referenced artifact

entries.purpose: POINTER/RECORD ONLY - this file does not change any contract byte. It records that a specific nested key inside the contract is superseded by its parent's marker, so that a reader who opens the sub-key alone does not mistakenly read it as the operative rule. Recommended shape: (a) treat the parent SUPERSEDED marker as covering the child, PLUS (b) name the child path here in an append-only file - which invalidates no existing hash and requires no re-anchoring.

remediationUpgrade.name: annotation upgrade (a-prime) proposed by schematic-expert
remediationUpgrade.problem: option (a) - a text prefix inside the value - is robust to key order, display order and deep-path reads, but a machine still has to parse prose to learn the state
remediationUpgrade.proposal: keep the human-readable prefix AND add a sibling machine-consumable key, e.g. disposition = '[SUPERSEDED - history only] add K48/K76 and RETAIN K109/K110 this batch; ...' plus dispositionStatus = {state: SUPERSEDED, operativeRule: 'REMOVE K109/K110 (t53)', note: 'retained as history only'}
benefits: a deep-path reader of the value carries the annotation with it
independent of key order and of sorted display
a program can consume the state without parsing prose
it only ADDS a key, so unlike renaming to disposition_superseded it breaks no existing deep-path reference
remediationUpgrade.criterionExtended: an annotation must be co-located with the content it constrains; state that must be machine-consumable must have its own field
remediationUpgrade.historyPreserved: the original disposition wording is retained (with the prefix), so the R1 convention still holds
remediationUpgrade.reportedToCaptain: the option set I already submitted listed (a)/(b)/(c)/status quo; this upgrade is offered as an amendment, since schematic-expert asked me to supplement rather than re-report
